query: How do you set boundaries without losing the relationship?
why_in_two_sentences: The #1 organic result (HelpGuide) fetched as navigation markup only, so the next organic article (BriteLife) was judged instead per the substitution rule. BriteLife matches the query's exact framing and supplies word-for-word scripts per relationship, which our page deliberately refuses to do, while ours is decisively deeper on why the ninety seconds after the sentence is the real skill; each page holds half of what the searcher wants.
what_the_winner_does_that_we_dont: Gives word-for-word scripts for specific situations: the constantly-venting friend, the late-night-conversation partner, privacy-crossing family, someone in active addiction
Defines a category of boundaries that protect the relationship itself (pause, repair, access, and role boundaries) rather than only protecting the self
Includes on-the-spot mini-scripts for the moment your mind goes blank
Simply Psychology adds a numbered five-step communication sequence: identify the need, choose the moment, direct language, state the consequence, follow through
what_we_do_that_they_dont: Explains why scripts fail when the underlying alarm is untouched, instead of handing over lines to memorize
Names the ninety seconds after the sentence as the actual skill and trains tolerance for the other person's reaction
Assigns their reaction to them and diagnoses the walkback and the smaller-version-offer five minutes later
34 verbatim FAQs covering in-laws, holidays, work, parents, and partners described as narcissists

above_the_fold.ours: H1 is the query, the short answer gives the limit-plus-ninety-seconds frame, then recognition sentences; strong, but it answers the fear abstractly.
above_the_fold.theirs: BriteLife's first paragraph mirrors the reader's exact catastrophic prediction (they'll get mad, you'll be the bad guy, you'll ruin everything) before any advice arrives.
above_the_fold.gap: Name the feared outcome explicitly in the first paragraph of the fold: that the reader pictures anger, rejection, or the relationship ending, and that the sentence is the easy half.

questions_they_answer_that_we_dont: How do I set boundaries with someone in active addiction or unstable behavior?
What do I actually say in the moment when my mind goes blank?
intent_mismatch: The query's without-losing-the-relationship half lives mostly in our FAQs, while BriteLife makes relationship preservation a headline section with its own boundary types.
trust_signals: BriteLife names an editor and writes from an addiction-recovery practice; Simply Psychology labels its draft AI-assisted but editorially reviewed; ours has no byline or sources.
one_change_with_most_traffic_impact: Add a short block of verbatim boundary sentences for the four most-searched relationships (partner, parent, friend, work); it is the one element both competitors lead with that our page argues against but never replaces with something usable.
